intro:
You are inside the real Agent Keyboard on agentkeyboard.com.

On a connected app, a prompt here opens a real coding session against that app's repo. It can edit, test, commit, and push while you watch. **This tour is prewritten:** no AI, owner credentials, or repo changes are used.

Pick a prompt and watch the real interface respond.

Ship a UI change.prompt: Make the hero headline bigger on phones, then verify it on mobile and desktop.
Ship a UI change.reply:
Done - increased the phone headline size, checked it at 390px and 1440px, committed as **Agent Keyboard**, and pushed `main`.

Your existing host sees the push and redeploys. That is the loop: ask from the app, change its repo, see the result in the same place.

Show the live work.prompt: Show me what you are doing while you work.
Show the live work.reply: The collapsed bar keeps a live ticker and timer. Expanded mode shows the prompt immediately, streamed assistant text, tool activity, a task checklist, and running sub-agents. You can collapse it or close the tab; the server keeps going.

Survive a restart.prompt: Keep this running if I close the tab or the Fly server restarts.
Survive a restart.reply: That is the fire-and-forget part. The job lives on the server, its id is saved before the browser can leave, and the bar re-attaches when you return. A self-triggered deploy can resume the same session after the machine comes back.

Undo the change.prompt: Roll back the last Agent Keyboard commit.
Undo the change.reply: Done - found the last Agent Keyboard commit, reverted it cleanly, and pushed the revert. Because every automated commit is attributed, the change is easy to identify in normal Git history.

stages.line: Finding the last Agent Keyboard commit

Talk, photos + files.prompt: Match the mobile spacing to this screenshot, use notes.pdf for the copy, and send - over and out.
Talk, photos + files.reply: Voice is transcribed live with `gpt-4o-transcribe`. Saying **over and out** removes the stop phrase, ends dictation, and sends. Photos, pasted images, and arbitrary files travel inline with the prompt; the agent can also return images in the transcript.

Try over and out.prompt: Make the cards easier to scan on mobile... over and out.
Try over and out.reply: The stop phrase is stripped before sending, so the agent receives: `Make the cards easier to scan on mobile.` No extra tap on the mic or send button.

Send while recording.prompt: I pressed Enter before stopping the recording.
Send while recording.reply: That works too. Enter flushes whatever has been transcribed so far, stops the recording behind the scenes, and sends it. Escape only stops dictation and leaves the prompt intact.

Show an inline image.prompt: Show me the reference image you used.
Show an inline image.reply: Images can appear in either direction. Tap a thumbnail to inspect it full-screen; the same transcript also keeps file markers and the prompt that went with them.

Steer the coding session.prompt: Switch to Sonnet, use high effort, enter plan mode, and set a goal for the pricing launch.
Steer the coding session.reply:
Session controls updated.

- Model: **Sonnet**
- Effort: **high**
- Permission mode: **plan**
- Goal: **launch the pricing page**

These are plain-English controls persisted per site, so there is no separate dashboard to babysit.

Compact the context.prompt: Compact the session so we have more context room.
Compact the context.reply: Compacted. The durable coding session keeps a concise summary of earlier work and frees room for the next turn. The transcript marks the compaction point instead of pretending the old context never existed.

Restart clean.reply: Restart stops active work, clears the coding context, discards uncommitted checkout changes, fetches origin, hard-resets to the latest configured branch, and removes untracked files. It only reports success when that real server action finishes.

Install a skill.prompt: Install image generation and use it to make a new hero asset.
Install a skill.reply: The server ships with useful skills already, and the agent can install more into its durable volume. A skill can add a specialized workflow such as image generation or browser verification, then use it in the same coding turn.

Ask how it works.prompt: What actually happens after I press send?
Ask how it works.reply: The widget sends your prompt to your small self-hosted server. That server syncs an allow-listed repo, resumes a durable Claude Code session in a fixed checkout, edits and verifies the app, commits as **Agent Keyboard**, and pushes. Your existing host deploys the push.

stages.line: Claude Code edits the allow-listed repo

What can it edit?.prompt: Is this only for static sites?
What can it edit?.reply: No. It edits the **codebase behind the app it sits on**. Static pages are an easy example, but the agent can work across frontend, backend, tests, configuration, and normal app architecture - whatever exists in the connected repo and can be shipped through Git.

Is it safe?.reply: Only sites in the server allow-list can be opened. The recommended GitHub token is fine-grained, limited to selected repos, and has no workflow permission; commits are attributed to **Agent Keyboard**. Invited editors share that server's repo access and the per-site coding session, so only invite trusted collaborators.

What does it cost?.prompt: What does this cost to run?
What does it cost?.reply: Mostly services you may already have: a Claude Code subscription does the editing, Supabase can handle auth on its free tier, and a small Fly machine hosts the durable server. An OpenAI key is optional and only used for voice transcription.

How do I install it?.prompt: How do I put this on my own apps?
How do I install it?.reply: Fork the MIT repo, configure your Supabase project, Fly app, Claude token, fine-grained GitHub token, and `SITES` allow-list, then add one script tag to each app. The self-hosting guide is written for a working setup in under an hour.
